main_text.l: ipsum. Quarta Raphaelis a tergo ejus. Majestas autem Sancti Benedicti est in medio. Ipse infidet throno excelso elevatus, atque soilium ejus sublime suspensum est furfum in aere. Figura autem gloriae ejus est sicuti color Chasmal, juxta illud, Ezechielis cap. 1. verf. 27. Et vidi quasi formam Chasmal. Corona impofita est capiti ejus, & diadema nominis Hammephorasch seu Tetragrammati circa frontem ejus, atque oculi per universum orbem discurrunt. Statuunt hos quatuor Angelos esse quam longissime remotos ab omni materia, nec ad tempus quidem aliquam induere materiam, hinc nunquam corporea specie videri, nec in terras venire, sed jugiter thronum DEI cingere, vocantes propterea illos Intelligentias a materia separatas; Quod tamen negare videtur Author Zennorennae, Commentarii in Legem, cum ad Genef. cap. 18. fol. 18. pronunciat Michaelem, Gabrielem, & Raphaelem e coelo in terram dimissos, ut Abrahamo, Lotho, Saraeque & divina annunciarent mandata, executionique mandarent; Sic autem legitur vocibus Hebraicis, Germanicisque: Da macht (Gott) drey Malachim (Engel) die kahmen zu Abraham, gleich als 3. Gäst: und die drey Malachim einer war Michael, der wolte sagen zu Sara, sie werde einen Sohn haben/und der Michael

page.notes: Marginal and hebrew text: the Hebrew words "נְחְמְרִים שְׂרָפִים" line is printed in Hebrew letters before "Intelligentias" and is not transcribed in full; the Hebrew phrase "הרבה מלאכים" appears in the line beginning "Intelligentias" and the Hebrew word "הקב" appears at the start of the German line "Da macht". Black letter German words are set in black letter and are rendered as printed in roman where uncertain. Two Hebrew phrases are doubtful and may be inexact.
